subject: maths
question: A and B can do a piece of work in 18 days, while A and C can do the same work in 12 days. If B and C together can complete the work in 48 days, how long will it take for A, B, and C working together to complete the work (rounded off to two decimal places)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM of 18, 12, and 48 = 144 units.

Efficiencies: (A + B) = 144 ÷ 18 = 8, (A + C) = 144 ÷ 12 = 12, (B + C) = 144 ÷ 48 = 3.

Combined efficiency of 2(A + B + C) = 8 + 12 + 3 = 23 units/day.

Efficiency of (A + B + C) = 23 ÷ 2 = 11.5 units/day.

Required time = 144 ÷ 11.5 ≈ 12.52 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.52 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A and B = 18 days

Time taken by A and C = 12 days

Time taken by B and C = 48 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of time taken

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Time Taken = Total Work ÷ Efficiency

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Efficiency of (A + B) + (A + C) + (B + C) = 8 + 12 + 3

⇒ Efficiency of 2(A + B + C) = 23 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of (A + B + C) = 23 ÷ 2 = 11.5 units/day

⇒ Time taken by A, B, and C together = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 144 ÷ 11.5

⇒ Time taken = 1440 ÷ 115

⇒ Time taken = 288 ÷ 23

⇒ Time taken ≈ 12.5217... days

**∴ The correct answer is 12.52 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns

Functions exactly like Time & Work. Filling pipes have positive efficiency, while emptying pipes (leaks) have negative efficiency.

Work & Wages

Wages are distributed in direct proportion to the amount of work done by each individual, which depends on their efficiency if they work for the same number of days.

Alternate Day Work

Calculate the total work done in a 2-day or 3-day cycle based on alternating individuals, then scale this cycle up to approach the total work without exceeding it.
